name: GA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -17 point partisan lean
Incumbent Andrew Clyde is running and holds a large fundraising edge
Democrat Caitlyn Gegen has minimal resources, about $4,700 on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at roughly 4 percent
model.rationale: This northeast Georgia seat leans heavily Republican, and Clyde enters as a well-funded incumbent while Gegen has raised only about $43,000. With no public polling and markets pricing the race at roughly 95 percent Republican, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Clyde win.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or a surge of outside spending against Clyde could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 9th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward the GOP. Andrew Clyde is seeking another term as the incumbent, holding a large financial advantage: he has raised roughly $671,000 and has outside groups both supporting and opposing him, while Democrat Caitlyn Gegen has raised about $43,000 with almost no cash on hand and no outside activity.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Clyde roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The forecast expects Clyde to win by a wide margin, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a competitive race.
